text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-President Hrawi criticises the press and what he called the laziness of the Lebanese people.
-Russian Foreign Minister Primakov in Beirut after meeting President Assad in Damascus; he says Israel is responsible for the faltering peace process.
-Foreign Minister Bouez says Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may resort to war as an exit from the worst situation he can find himself in.
-Prosecutor-general Addoum says the "mafia" is behind sending the plastic waste to Lebanon.
-A hundred soldiers from Estonia will arrive in Lebanon soon to receive military training from the Norwegian peacekeepers of UNIFIL.
-The European Union to grant Lebanon $48 million to help finance the cost of administrative reform.
-Primakov met President Hrawi and Prime Minister Hariri and signed a cooperation protocol with Bouez between Lebanon and Russia.
-Hrawi says the new government will be formed within two days.

-Fourteen years after the assassination of president-elect Bashir Gemayel, an investigating judge demands the death penalty in an indictment for two men charged with carrying out the bombing that killed Gemayel and 23 others.
-Prosecutor Addoum: "Germany will inform Lebanon of its position on the plastic waste within 48 hours".
-Israeli army officers visit the Jezzine area north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
